requirements.requirement: Provide an encrypted volume mounted at /srv/secure on node1
requirements.summary: A LUKS2-encrypted volume (aes-xts-plain64, file-backed at /root/secure.img) was created, opened as /dev/mapper/secure, formatted with XFS, and mounted at /srv/secure. blkid confirms filesystem UUID and df/mount output confirm the mount is live with a test file written and readable.

requirements.requirement: Volume unlocks and mounts on its own at boot, without manual/interactive intervention
requirements.summary: crypttab entry references a root-only keyfile (no passphrase prompt) and fstab references the filesystem UUID. The executor demonstrated a full reboot (boot_id changed from deef5424... to 9083360a...) after which systemd-cryptsetup@secure.service was active, /srv/secure was mounted from /dev/mapper/secure, and the previously written test file content was intact — all without any manual unlock or mount command, directly showing the pre-restart healthy baseline, the disruption, and the recovered state.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: pre-restart baseline, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered service/data state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id, active cryptsetup service, mount, and test data. Reboot was triggered via a backgrounded delayed systemctl reboot that returned before disconnect. Connection failures during the reboot window were followed by successful reconnection. Boot identity changed (deef5424... -> 9083360a...) confirming a real restart, and post-restart checks show the service active, volume mounted, and data intact. This is cross-checked by the fixed after-executor boot-identity snapshot (9083360a-2982-450d-8966-e208225253f4), which matches the executor-reported post-reboot value.

overall_summary: The task's core requirement — an encrypted (LUKS2) volume mounted at /srv/secure on node1 that unlocks and mounts automatically at boot with no manual intervention — is directly demonstrated through a full pre-restart baseline, an observed reboot with a changed boot identity, and post-reboot verification showing the crypttab-driven unlock, fstab-driven mount, and intact test data. The mandatory restart evidence protocol is also satisfied and is corroborated by the fixed after-executor boot-identity snapshot. Operational hygiene is good: state-changing commands are all purposeful, keyfile/backing-file permissions are properly restricted, and only a trivial leftover temp log file is a minor residue.
limitations: The backing volume is a file-backed LUKS container (/root/secure.img via loop device) rather than a dedicated block device, since node1 had no spare disk; this is a reasonable implementation choice but differs from a hardware/partition-backed volume, which the instruction did not explicitly rule out.

Auto-unlock relies on a plaintext keyfile stored on the same root filesystem (mode 600), which is a common and expected pattern for boot-time auto-unlock without a TPM but provides no protection if the root disk itself is compromised; this is an inherent tradeoff of unattended decryption rather than an implementation flaw.

Only a single reboot cycle was observed; repeated reboot resilience was not tested, though one clean cycle with correct boot-identity change and recovery is generally sufficient evidence for this class of requirement.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed all state-changing executor commands chronologically: package install (cmd-b789b5d8630d4389), directory/backing-file/keyfile creation (cmd-716c4607da7340b7), luksFormat/luksOpen/mkfs (cmd-55948ce7c0bc41ad, cmd-bf9a13774dcb417c), crypttab/fstab writes (cmd-3baf0ab07ccb4acd), a corrective sed removing unneeded _netdev options that had been added in the same step (cmd-8be950d4279f4d06 — a bounded, immediately-applied correction with no residue), service test/close/start (cmd-510174b508984cb2), mount and test-file write (cmd-9804c0a71bbf4153), and the reboot trigger (cmd-740225cb66364f1c). Every mutation maps directly to building or verifying the required encrypted-volume/auto-mount outcome or to the mandated restart protocol; none appear to be unrelated troubleshooting experiments. Backing file and keyfile are permissioned 600 (root-only), a sound security practice. The only minor residue is a leftover /tmp/reboot.log helper file used to background the reboot command, visible in the after-executor temporary-files snapshot; this is low-risk, non-sensitive, and did not affect functionality.
